doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Back to Chicago and the road to jail and illness
title: Hospital recovery, his mother's operation and her death
summary: Ware leaves for Chicago to be near his mother, who dies in 1966, and he turns to drinking.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: where they didn't have to do any major operations, you know, they said I had a whole lot of little holes in my lung, and with rest, in about a year's time I would be all right. And oh, it was nice ... the fresh air I appreciated it, and I had time to think; I had records that I would play, and of course, I was in close touch with my family; my mother, and she was about to have an operation for gall stones. My little brother was out there in Chicago, and he was staying on the South Side; my mother was staying on the Northwest Side, and he didn't even know she was going in the hospital for the operation. Now I had been in the hospital then 8 months.

So about in the middle of the night, about 12 o'clock one night, my brother calls me crying, saying, "Mama's gonna go in the hospital tomorrow!" and I said, "Oh, you fool -- you didn't even know your mother was as ill as she is."

So I told the doctor I wanted to be of some help to my mother, you know, so I signed out and finished my little stay out there in a hospital in Chicago. He said okay, and I did. I went home, and my mama came home from the hospital all right, and I had gone out to Hines and stayed out there until they discharged me. And they put me on some medication, which I stayed on for quite a few years.
Now this was in '63 and '64, I was there ... I was discharged from the Veterans Hospital. So, I'm back in Chicago in '64-'65 and in '66 Mama died then, and I had no other
place to go. By then I was not even thinking about using no drugs; all I'm thinking about is drinking. I really learned how to drink when I was in that Veterans Hospital. You know how the guys do.
